topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture’s subject and objectives before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Mutation and clonal evolution in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations from different sources contribute to cancer arising through clonal evolution in a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Evidence and debate about environmental cancer risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and interpretation surrounding environmental contributions to cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain infection-related carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a specific example.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage through their distinct molecular mechanisms.

topics.label: Tissue context in tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tissue conditions shape carcinogenesis, ending with a summary of carcinogenic mechanisms and tissue specificity.

topics.label: Exposure evidence and epidemiological assessment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological evidence of exposure supports the assessment of carcinogenicity in human populations.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity and mutagenicity testing
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine experimental tests used to assess carcinogenic potential and the limitations of their results.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by reviewing its main findings and their relevance to risk–benefit decisions.
